title: "06 · Downloading a street network"
execute:
  enabled: false
---

Get a street network in, clean it, know what you have. The other four OSMnx
notebooks assume it.

The same neighborhood downloaded as `drive`, `bike`, `walk` and `all` gives
243, 814, 1582 and 1894 intersections, and comparing their lengths naively
inflates the walk-to-drive ratio from 2.4× to 4.6×, because summing a directed
multigraph double-counts two-way streets and a drive network here is 98 %
one-way. Simplification removes 79 % of the nodes without changing a meter of
length; consolidation at a 40 m tolerance moves one node 302 m, since a chain of
intersections collapses to a point that need not lie near any of its members.

Several operators are wrong, and the notebook says so where it meets them: a
bounding box passed in the wrong order silently reduces a 243-node network to 2
while reporting success, a cache key omits the radius so six downloads overwrite
one file, and a family of cleaning operators replace the graph and never rebuild
the mesh you are looking at.
